A Non-Root User, and .dockerignore

USER node costs one line because the official image already ships the user; .dockerignore keeps the build context to what the image actually needs.

A container image built with no USER instruction runs as root by default — meaning a bug or a dependency vulnerability that lets an attacker execute arbitrary code in this process hands them root inside the container as a bonus, for no benefit this API actually needs (it never writes to the filesystem, binds a privileged port, or does anything else that requires elevated permissions). The Dockerfile's USER node line, right before EXPOSE, switches to a non-root user for every instruction after it — one line, not a new user to create, because the official node:22-alpine image already ships a node user built in.

.dockerignore works like .gitignore, but for what gets sent to Docker as the build context — every COPY in the Dockerfile can only reach files Docker actually received:

# Figure 6.20: .dockerignore (excerpt)
node_modules/
.git/
.env
.env.*
!.env.example

content/
tutorial/
dist/
tests/

node_modules/ matters most: without it, Docker would upload the host's own node_modules (platform-specific native bindings included) only to have npm ci inside the image overwrite it anyway — pure wasted transfer. The rest excludes what CLAUDE.md already establishes has no business in a running container at all: content/ (never even reaches students, per CLAUDE.md's "Students never receive content/"), the tutorial's own toolchain, and test files this image never runs.
